To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variance decay of a conserved passive scalar in decaying isotropic turbulence follows a power law with an exponent alpha that is determined by the initial length-scale ratio and that the probability density function of the scalar relaxes toward a Dirac delta function with a rate that is determined by lambda.

a stochastic model for mixing in decaying turbulence based on the law large numbers is presented and it is shown to reproduce the power law behavior for the decay of variance of the conserved scalar in a good agreement.
the mixing parameter lambda is a crucial factor for the decay of the scalar variance in a decaying turbulent mixing process.

the decay of scalar variance in decaying turbulence can be described by a power law, with the exponent alpha depending on the initial length scale ratio of the velocity to the scalar field, lambda.
